Subject: Candidate Carmen Gonzalez - request for immigration/relocation exception (offer attached)

Hi Lauren,

Following up on Carmen Gonzalez (ex-HSBC, L4 SWE) — she’s completed interviews and we’re ready to extend an offer at the top of band (Base $165k, target 15% bonus). Carmen has a non-standard immigration/relocation situation: her spouse’s open work authorization will be delayed ~6 months, which increases household risk if she relocates. Carmen asked whether Redwood can offer an immigration/legal stipend to cover work-permit assistance and a larger up-front relocation to bridge the gap.

Attached: offer_summary.pdf and relocation_estimate.xlsx (vendor estimate from ReloPro). Current standard policy: up to $5k lump-sum relocation for L4 and no routine immigration stipend. Candidate is asking for $9k relocation + $6k immigration/legal support.

As discussed with BrightHire, this is borderline for policy — she is a high-priority hire for payments infra team and Vivek recommended we consider an exception if we can get headcount and a one-time approval.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm headcount is green for FY26 H2 (JIRA-HEADCOUNT-4127)?
- Approve exceptional package (proposed: $8k relocation reimbursed, $6k immigration stipend paid as lump-sum upon start; itemized receipts required)
- If approved, I’ll route updated offer via DocuSign and include finance / payroll guidance for coding.

Thanks — trying to get a signed offer before the end of next week.

Best,
Tessa
Talent Partner
Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for the write-up and the attachments. I pulled the JIRA headcount ticket and FYI headcount is available under the infra hiring plan approved on 2026-06-01. I’m comfortable with the proposed base and bonus inside the comp band for L4.

Two items I need before I can greenlight an exception:
1) Brief business justification (1-2 lines) on why this hire requires an above-policy relocation/immigration package rather than retaining in a remote location. Please call out the role-specific ramp needs that require onsite presence.
2) Confirmation on how this will be coded in finance (capitalized or hiring expense) and whether payroll can process a lump-sum stipend (Monica, please advise).

If those are fine, I’m inclined to approve up to the amounts you suggested, conditional on Carmen signing by 2026-08-10 and providing receipts. If Vivek wants to escalate for a larger sign-on or alternative structure (sign-on + stipend), flag it here.

Lauren
VP, Engineering (Payments)
Redwood Inference

Lauren / Tessa — I reviewed the comp and the team case. Carmen was the strongest candidate; ramp timeline and domain knowledge are important for the payments roadmap. I approve an exception as follows:

- Immigration/legal stipend: one-time $6,000 (paid as a taxable lump-sum on first payroll).
- Relocation reimbursement: up to $8,000 (vendor or receipts), paid after move with receipts; ReloPro estimate looks reasonable.
- Sign-on: no additional sign-on beyond standard L4 unless exceptional competitor counter-offer emerges; escalate to me if needed.
- Conditions: Must sign offer by 2026-08-10; receipts and vendor invoices required; if employee leaves within 12 months, reimbursement pro-rata recoupment applies per policy.

Monica — can HR/Finance please confirm whether we run the stipend through payroll (taxable) and whether relocation can be coded to the hiring pool? If not, advise alternate routing.
